attrs.description:
Picks an Anima ControlNet-LLLite weights file and outputs the filename as a
combo, so it can drive the Anima LLLite Tiled ControlNet Sampler's
``lllite_name``. Lets you choose the LLLite model once and route it
into one or more samplers.

It only outputs the filename — the actual LLLite module is built against the
model inside the sampler — so it has no dependency on any other node pack.

attrs.tooltip: Anima ControlNet-LLLite weights file (from the controlnet folder).

per_tile: sample each tile fully then stitch (lowest VRAM; can show seams/ghosting). multidiffusion: one sampling pass over the whole image, averaging overlapping tiles in latent space every step — tiles stay in sync so seams and double-exposure are eliminated (slightly more VRAM). In multidiffusion mode the 'method' and 'color_match' fields are not used.
Anima ControlNet-LLLite weights file (from the controlnet folder).
Delegate to any model_function_wrapper already installed upstream instead of overwriting it, so multiple wrapper nodes can stack. Same toggle as the AnimaLLLiteApply node.
Overlap between tiles as a fraction of tile size, added on top of overlap_x/overlap_y.
Extra horizontal overlap in pixels.
Extra vertical overlap in pixels.
Resampling used to keep every decoded tile at a uniform size before stitching.

Per-tile color matching against the source tile, to fix tonal seams (brightness/colour steps between tiles). 'mean_std' re-scales each tile's per-channel mean/std (fast, simple); 'wavelet' keeps the tile's detail but takes the source tile's broad tone (better on textured tiles).
How strongly to apply the color match (0 = off, 1 = full).

(multidiffusion only) Decode the final full-image latent in tiles instead of one pass, to avoid a single huge VAE decode that can spike VRAM (or spill into slow shared system memory). No effect in per_tile mode, where each tile is already decoded on its own.
(multidiffusion only) Tile size in pixels for the tiled VAE decode.

attrs.display_name: Power Lora Loader to Prompt (Image Saver)

attrs.tooltip: When enabled, the trigger lookup crosses subgraph boundaries (inbound and outbound) until it reaches a real node, instead of stopping at the boundary.
When enabled, this node also mirrors its OWN bypass/mute state onto the downstream node(s): if this node is bypassed/muted, the output node is too. Its own state takes precedence over the trigger.
The image you want to insert (e.g. pose, object, decal).
Defines where the image will be placed. The white area determines the bounding box.
fit scales the image inside the mask’s box (no crop). fill covers the box completely (may crop edges).
Alignment on the x axis of the fitted image inside the box if the aspect ratio doesn’t match perfectly.
Alignment on the y axis of the fitted image inside the box if the aspect ratio doesn’t match perfectly.
Manual pixel offset on the x axis for fine-tuning the placement.
Manual pixel offset on the y axis for fine-tuning the placement.
Mask brightness threshold for detecting the box. 0.5 works for most cases.
Expands the bounding box outward by N pixels.
If true, respects transparency in the source image during paste.
Resampling method used when resizing the source image.
The image you’re compositing onto. If not provided, a blank canvas is created.
Canvas width when no destination image is given.
Canvas height when no destination image is given.
How many original pixels make up one pixel-art pixel. 8 on a 512px image → 64×64 pixel grid.
Max palette size when using Auto or Grayscale palette.
Box averages each pixel block before quantizing (better color). Nearest samples a single pixel (harder, more aliased).
Scale the pixel grid back to the original image size using nearest-neighbor so each pixel block is clearly visible. Disable to output the raw low-resolution pixel art.

attrs.description: FaceDetailer clone that asks for one prompt per detected segment.

attrs.tooltip: Base positive conditioning. Used for every segment whose dialog prompt is left empty.
Order in which segments are numbered in the dialog and processed.
How long to wait for the dialog before applying the timeout policy. 0 = wait forever. Keep > 0 if you also run workflows headless via the API.
When enabled, the node re-executes (and re-asks) on every run even if inputs are unchanged. When disabled, unchanged inputs reuse the cached result without showing the dialog.

attrs.tooltip: Denoise strength. For a tiled hires-fix on an already-upscaled image keep this low (e.g. 0.3-0.5).
Overlap between tiles as a fraction of tile size, added on top of overlap_x/overlap_y.

Decode the final full-image latent in tiles instead of one pass, to avoid a single huge VAE decode that can spike VRAM (or, on Windows, spill into slow shared system memory). The decode is a single full-image pass independent of rows/columns, so adding tiles won't shrink it - enable this instead.
Tile size in pixels for the tiled VAE decode.

attrs.description: VAEDecode with a batch_size field to decode fewer latents at a time.

attrs.tooltip: The latent to be decoded.
The VAE model used for decoding the latent.

How many latents to hand to the VAE per decode call. Lower values reduce peak VRAM at the cost of more sequential calls; the default of 1 decodes one image at a time. Values >= the batch size behave exactly like the built-in node (single decode).
The decoded image.
